_about: Trials whose owner the evidence contests, for the PI to rule on (like AT-AP-SLK-05-I13-I14). The primary scores keep the committed owners; the report also gives the scores under each reading. Found 2026-09-27 while scoring sources 1 and 3.

cases.question: Is a failure the mock's when an ignored filter returned the item, but the response also showed the filter was not applied?
cases.committed_owner: agent (labelled 2026-09-25, before the replica notes documented the ignored parent filter)
cases.sources_against: judge v1 on Muse and on Sonnet (artifact, 'ignored parent filter'); the counterfactual trace scan
cases.mechanism: The agent asked for issues(filter: {parent: {id: {eq: "i-epic"}}}). The replica ignores `parent` (verified: apply_issue_filter handles no `parent` key) and returned every issue. The agent marked Done an issue that is not a child of the epic (WEB-4, a grandchild; WEB-6, a child of Checkout analytics). Real Linear would not have returned it.
cases.reading_mock: The rule applied in Phase 1 from 2026-09-27 00:40 ('an ignored filter decided the outcome') makes these the mock's: the agent trusted the server's filter.
cases.reading_agent: The response listed the parent issue itself among its own sub-issues, which a working filter cannot return. In t1 the agent even remarked 'this is the parent itself, not a sub-issue' and still trusted the rest.

cases.question: When an ignored filter introduced the item, does it matter whether the agent noticed the mismatch before acting?
cases.committed_owner: as listed: the labels separate trusting the filter (mock) from noticing the mismatch and acting anyway (agent)
cases.sources_against: the counterfactual trace scan flags all four (the ignored filter introduced the item in each); judge v2 agrees with the labels on the two it judged, but those two labels were revised after v2's verdicts
cases.mechanism: Box search ignores content_types; Slack users.conversations ignores types. In every trial the item first reached the agent in a response the real service would not have given. In AT-BOX-23-I11 t1 the agent called the description mismatch 'odd' and trusted the filter; in t3 it read the mismatch and took the file as 'the only candidate'. In P-SLK-23-I13 t3 it said the channel is public and acted anyway.
cases.reading_mock: The counterfactual: against the real service the agent would not have seen the item at that point, so any such failure is the mock's.
cases.reading_agent: The labels: only reliance on the filter makes it the mock's; an agent that saw the item fails the request and acted anyway failed on its own.

cases.question: Is 'Linear has no documents' the agent's error when the harness's API documentation lists no documents operation?
cases.committed_owner: agent (override); its stated reason said the solver's prompt names no endpoints, which is wrong
cases.sources_against: none of the sources flags them; found while checking the override's facts
cases.mechanism: The benchmark's own system prompt lists 19 Linear operations (teams, issues, issueUpdate, comments, ...) and none for documents or projects. The replica serves documents; `projects` queries fail. In t5 the agent tried `projects` twice, got the replica's error, and concluded that projects and documents are unsupported; in the other two it concluded so without a call. All three are not_established (the facts were never tested).
cases.reading_agent: The listing is not exhaustive, real Linear has documents, and the replica notes expect agents to discover the rest by trying or by introspection.
cases.reading_harness_or_test: The agent followed the harness's documentation; a test that needs an operation the harness does not document tests the documentation, not the fact. (For t5, the replica's failing projects query also contributed.)

cases.question: Under the PI's natural-ambiguity ruling (2026-09-27), which of the 7 test-wording tests are valid?
trials: the 19 trials owned by test-wording: U-BOX-23-File_extension, U-CAL-23-EventAttendee_email, U-CAL-23-EventAttendee_optional, U-LIN-24-Cycle_number, U-AP2-CAL-02-CalendarListEntry_calendar_id, H-BOX-31-I11, P-BOX-31-I11
cases.committed_owner: test-wording (labels written before the ruling, as 'defective test' or 'invalid test')
cases.sources_against: the Muse objection reader (source 4) reads 12 of the 19 trials as natural ambiguity (9) or solver error (3)
cases.mechanism: Examples of the reader's readings: 'Architecture review: storage' is still an architecture review, so both Friday reviews match; 'about travel costs' most naturally attaches to the comment, not the spreadsheet; nothing in 'the contract file' excludes the second PDF.
cases.reading_agent: The ruling: misreading a natural request is the agent's failure, perhaps a weaker one.
cases.reading_test: The labels: the solver's reading is at least as natural as the author's, so the trial shows no mistake.
